content: Completeness of the Information Dictionary: In this step, the system validates the completeness of the ID, which is defined by the number of obligatory slots filled in the information dictionary. There are 6 distinct cases when the ID is considered to be complete (see Section SECREF13 of the Appendix). For instance, if a user works on a final examination, the system does not has to request a sub-topic or examination level. Thus, the ID has to be filled only with data for a topic, examination mode, and question number, whereas, if the user works on a quiz, the system has to gather information about the topic, sub-topic, examination mode, and the question number. Once the ID is complete, it is provided to the verification step. Otherwise, the system proceeds according to the next action. The system extracts the information in each dialogue step, and thus if the user provides updated information on any subject later in the dialogue, the corresponding slot will be updated in the ID.
